topics.name: Interrupts
topics.description: Pausing a graph for human input.
notes: - 在节点中调用 interrupt() 暂停图的执行，等待人工输入。
- 必须配置 checkpointer，才能保存暂停时的状态。
- 典型场景：审批工具调用、人工修改草稿、补充缺失信息。

topics.name: Resuming Execution
notes: - 使用相同的 thread_id，并用 Command(resume=...) 传入人工的回复继续运行。
- 恢复时被中断的节点会从头重新执行，interrupt() 返回人工提供的值，所以中断前的代码应避免副作用。

questions.title: What must be configured for interrupt() to work?

options.text: A checkpointer, so the paused state can be saved
A vector store
A second model
A LangSmith API key

questions.explanation: The graph state is persisted when it pauses and loaded again on resume, which requires a checkpointer.

questions.title: Which are typical human-in-the-loop use cases?

options.text: Approving a tool call before it runs
Reviewing or editing a draft written by the model
Asking the user for missing information
Making model inference faster

questions.explanation: Interrupts add a human decision point. They do not speed up inference.

questions.title: What happens when this node first reaches interrupt(...)?

options.text: Execution pauses and the payload is surfaced to the caller
It prints the question and waits on standard input
It returns None immediately and continues
It raises an exception that permanently ends the graph

questions.explanation: The run stops at the interrupt and the payload is returned to the caller. The graph continues when the caller resumes with a value.

questions.title: Fill in the type used to resume a paused run.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langgraph.types import Command

graph.invoke(______(resume="yes"), config)

options.text: Command
Resume
Continue
Send

questions.explanation: Command(resume=value) supplies the human answer that interrupt() returns.

questions.title: When a run is resumed, which part of the interrupted node executes again?

options.text: The whole node runs again from its beginning
Only the lines after interrupt()
Nothing, the node is skipped
The previous node

questions.explanation: The node restarts and interrupt() now returns the resume value instead of pausing.

questions.title: Why should code before interrupt() avoid side effects such as sending an email?

options.text: Because the node re-runs on resume and the side effect would happen twice
Because interrupt() deletes earlier output
Because side effects are not allowed in LangGraph
Because checkpoints cannot store emails

questions.explanation: Put side effects after the interrupt, or make them idempotent.

questions.title: The resume call does not continue the paused run. What is wrong?

options.text: The resume call uses a different thread_id, so the paused state is not found
resume must be a number
Command cannot be passed to invoke
The first call must use stream() instead

questions.explanation: The paused state lives in the thread where it was interrupted. Resume with the same thread_id.
